instructions: At least 2 hours before dinner, or the night before, make the dough. In a large bowl, stir together 3 cups of the flour, the 2 1/4 tsp yeast, 1 tsp sugar and the 1 1/4 tsp salt.
Pour in 1 cup plus 2 tbsp warm tap water and 2 tbsp of the olive oil. Stir with a wooden spoon until there's no dry flour left. It'll look shaggy and a little sticky.
Dust the counter with a little of the last 1/4 cup flour and transfer the dough out. Knead it for 5 minutes, until it's smooth and springs back slowly when you poke it.

Put it back in the bowl, cover it with plastic wrap and leave it somewhere warm for 1 1/2 to 2 hours, until it's doubled. If you're making it the night before, put the covered bowl in the fridge once it's doubled and take it out 1 hour before you shape it.
About 45 minutes before you want to eat, put a large baking sheet upside down on the lowest rack, or a pizza stone if you have one, and heat the oven to 500°F. Give it a full 30 minutes to get hot.
Meanwhile, grate the 12 oz mozzarella (about 3 cups) and 1/4 cup of the Parmesan.
Melt the 1 tbsp butter in a small bowl in the microwave, about 20 seconds. Stir in the last 1 tbsp olive oil and the 1/4 tsp garlic powder.
Put the 1 tsp red pepper flakes in a small bowl for the table.
Taste the pizza sauce. If it's flat, stir in a pinch of salt.
Transfer the dough onto the floured counter and cut it in half. Shape each half into a ball and cover one with a clean kitchen towel.

Lay a sheet of parchment on the counter and press the other ball flat on it. Stretch it out from the middle with your fingertips into a 12 inch round, leaving the outer 1/2 inch a little thicker. If it keeps shrinking back, leave it for 5 minutes and try again.

Spread 1/2 cup of the sauce over it with the back of a spoon, leaving a 1 inch border bare. Scatter over half the mozzarella, 1 tbsp of the Parmesan and 1/4 tsp of the Italian seasoning. Lay half the pepperoni over the top.
Brush the bare border with half the garlic butter and sprinkle it with 1 tbsp of the Parmesan.

Slide the pizza on its parchment onto the hot baking sheet. Bake for 8 to 11 minutes, until the crust is deep golden, the cheese is bubbling with brown spots and the edges of the pepperoni have curled up and crisped.
While it bakes, stretch and top the second pizza the same way on a fresh sheet of parchment, with the rest of the sauce, mozzarella, Italian seasoning, pepperoni, garlic butter and Parmesan.
Slide the first pizza onto a cutting board and pull out the parchment. Put the second pizza in to bake the same way.
Let the first pizza sit for 2 minutes, then cut it into 8 slices. Cut the second one the same way when it comes out.
Serve with the red pepper flakes on the side.
advance_prep_notes: make the dough at least 2 hours ahead so it has time to rise, or the night before and keep it in the fridge
method_notes: Both read versions make a yeasted dough, let it rise until doubled, stretch it by hand rather than rolling it and bake it on a preheated stone or pan in a very hot oven with sauce, mozzarella and pepperoni. Oh Sweet Basil (the lead, and the only one with 20 or more ratings) makes a big batch of dough that keeps in the fridge for days, heats the pan at 500°F to 550°F, uses only a little sauce, adds Parmesan and Italian seasoning under the pepperoni and brushes the crust with butter, olive oil, Parmesan and garlic salt before a 6 to 8 minute bake. Lauren's Latest makes two 12 inch pizzas from 3 cups of bread flour, uses more sauce and cheese and bakes them at 475°F for 9 to 12 minutes. This one makes two 12 inch pizzas from a dough the size of Lauren's Latest and finishes the crust the lead's way, with garlic powder in place of garlic salt.
